genesis.25.p1.b1.text: Now Abraham had taken another wife, named Keturah,

genesis.25.p1.b2.text: and she bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. … All these were descendants of Keturah.

genesis.25.p1.b3.text: Abraham left everything he owned to Isaac.

genesis.25.p1.b4.text: But while he was still alive, Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them away from his son Isaac to the land of the east.

genesis.25.p2.b5.text: Abraham lived a total of 175 years. And at a ripe old age he breathed his last and died, old and contented, and was gathered to his people.

genesis.25.p2.b6.text: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah …

genesis.25.p2.b7.text: Abraham was buried there with his wife Sarah.

genesis.25.p2.b8.text: After Abraham’s death, God blessed his son Isaac, who lived near Beer-lahai-roi.

genesis.25.p3.b9.text: This is the account of Abraham’s son Ishmael, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s maidservant, bore to Abraham.

genesis.25.p3.b10.text: These were the sons of Ishmael, and these were their names by their villages and encampments—twelve princes of their tribes.

genesis.25.p3.b11.text: Ishmael’s descendants settled from Havilah to Shur, which is near the border of Egypt as you go toward Asshur. And they lived in hostility toward all their brothers.

genesis.25.p3.b12.text: Ishmael lived a total of 137 years. Then he breathed his last and died …

genesis.25.p4.b13.text: Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah …

genesis.25.p4.b14.text: Later, Isaac prayed to the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was barren. And the LORD heard his prayer …

genesis.25.p4.b15.text: Why is this happening to me?

genesis.25.p4.b16.text: Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you will be separated; one people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.

genesis.25.p5.b17.text: The first one came out red, covered with hair like a fur coat; so they named him Esau.

genesis.25.p5.b18.text: After this, his brother came out grasping Esau’s heel; so he was named Jacob.

genesis.25.p5.b19.text: And Isaac was sixty years old when the twins were born.

genesis.25.p6.b20.text: When the boys grew up, Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the field,

genesis.25.p6.b21.text: while Jacob was a quiet man who stayed at home.

genesis.25.p6.b22.text: Because Isaac had a taste for wild game, he loved Esau; but Rebekah loved Jacob.

genesis.25.p7.b23.text: One day, while Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came in from the field and was famished.

genesis.25.p7.b24.text: Let me eat some of that red stew, for I am famished.

genesis.25.p8.b26.text: I am about to die, so what good is a birthright to me?

genesis.25.p8.b28.text: So Esau swore to Jacob and sold him the birthright.

genesis.25.p8.b29.text: … who ate and drank and then got up and went away. Thus Esau despised his birthright.
